- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- Model underreacts to recent price declines; fails to adjust downward when recent history shows weakening momentum.
- Overestimates volatility in the short term, particularly after sharp spikes; forecasts overshoot and then correct too aggressively.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model assumes prices will return to historical averages too quickly, ignoring structural or policy-driven trends.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends; model is slow to catch momentum.
- When true price rises sharply, model often fails to anticipate the magnitude, leading to underestimation of peak prices.
- Model exhibits “anchoring” bias — overweights recent high prices and underweights low prices in the history window, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to short-term noise; smoothing or averaging recent history helps reduce overfitting to volatility.
